title: Read a payment batch from a CSV file

intent.outcome: Ledgerline reads a batch of payments from a CSV file
intent.problem: the batch arrived as a spreadsheet nobody could script against

acceptance_criteria.description: a batch of ten payments is read
acceptance_criteria.verification: grep -c ',' fixtures/batches.csv && echo "the batch file has rows"

evidence.command: grep -c ',' fixtures/batches.csv && echo "the batch file has rows"

steps.action: parse the CSV into a batch

rounds.notes: Two defects in the reader; D1 stops the release.

findings.description:
## D1 [high] The reader stops at the first blank line

**where:** `ledgerline-core/src/batch.rs`

**defect:** a blank line ends the batch, so every payment after it is dropped.

**scenario:** import a batch with a blank line between two payments.

**fix:** skip blank lines until the end of the file.
findings.resolution: blank lines are skipped; the reader runs to the end of the file

comments.author: sam
comments.body: re-checked the batch with a blank line: every payment is read

findings.description:
## D2 [low] The header row is counted as a payment

**where:** `ledgerline-core/src/batch.rs`

**defect:** the header is parsed into the batch, so the count is one too high.

**scenario:** import any batch and count the payments.

**fix:** start at the first line after the header.
findings.resolution: the header is read as the column names; the count is right

questions.question: Do we keep the amount in pence or convert on import?
questions.answer: pence, converted once at the edge

notes.author: thea
notes.body: the gateway sends amounts in pence; keep the conversion in one place
